assets.prompt: A game sprite of Shiloh Meeting House, an unadorned one-room hewn-log Methodist chapel in rural Tennessee in 1862. Steep weathered wood-shingle gable roof, plain doorway in the gable end, small square shuttered opening on long side, notched horizontal logs on low stone supports. No chimney, steeple, bell, cross or porch. Full building, three-quarter bird's-eye view looking down at 60 degrees. Crisp realistic painterly miniature, daylight from upper left, muted gray-brown timber. Centered with generous transparent margins. Transparent background PNG cutout with genuine alpha, tight contact shadow. No landscape or objects around the building.

Single transparent PNG game sprite, Chancellor House at Chancellorsville in May 1863: broad two-and-a-half-story red-brick Virginia rural tavern house with a long seven-bay facade, white sash windows, dark brown wood-shingle gabled roof with three modest dormers, brick chimneys at the ends and central roof, a small plain white central porch and a taller rear wing. No grand colonnade. Historically informed illustrative reconstruction. Bird's-eye three-quarter view from 60 degrees overhead, whole building visible, refined realistic miniature painting, muted brick and timber, upper-left daylight. Building centered with 15 percent empty TRANSPARENT margin. No shadow, no glow, no halo, no haze, no vignette, no floor, no surrounding objects. Genuine transparent RGBA background cutout.

Transparent PNG cutout sprite of a small Brotherton farm log cabin at Chickamauga, Georgia, September 1863: squat single-pen near-square hewn-log dwelling, squared weathered gray-brown logs with muted ochre clay chinking and dovetail corner joints, low continuous stone foundation, simple plank doorway in the long wall, steep wood-shingle side-gabled roof, one large external irregular stone chimney at the gable end partly sheltered by the extended eave. Historically informed illustrative reconstruction, not a claim of exact surviving 1863 fabric. No porch or modern visitor gate. High bird's-eye three-quarter view looking down 60 degrees, entire cabin including stone chimney visible. Crisp realistic painted miniature, soft light from upper left, subdued timber and gray stone. One building centered, generous fully transparent margin, only a very small contact shadow. Genuine alpha PNG cutout; no landscape, ground tile, people, flags, lettering or frame.

rejectedAttempts.initialPrompt: Use case: historical-scene. Create one finished transparent PNG sprite for an overhead American Civil War tactical game: the simple log Shiloh Meeting House in April 1862. The attached A. M. Connett painting in the NPS collection is architectural reference ONLY. Reconstruct the single-room rectangular log meetinghouse: hewn horizontal weathered light-brown logs, corner notches, plain steep wood-shingle gabled roof, simple doorway at the short gable end and a small square shuttered opening on the long side. No steeple, cross, bell tower, porch, chimney, masonry church or modern features. Change the painting viewpoint to a bird's-eye three-quarter overhead camera about 60 degrees down, so the complete roof and front and right walls can be read. Realistic painterly miniature, crisp wood grain and shingles, subdued rural colors, soft light from upper left, matches refined Civil War battlefield unit sprites. Building alone centered and complete, generous 12% transparent margins, tight subtle contact shadow. Genuinely transparent alpha background. No ground tile, grass, trees, people, flags, text, signs, border or extra buildings. Preserve the humble massing from the reference rather than inventing a grand church.
rejectedAttempts.editPrompt: Edit this Shiloh Meeting House sprite. Remove the ENTIRE gray-white checkerboard background and ALL background grid patterns. Replace them with actual transparent alpha pixels in an RGBA PNG, not a painted transparency pattern, not white or black. Preserve the building exactly: same log walls, window, door, shingle roof, size, angle, colors and position. Retain only a very tight soft contact shadow immediately under the building, with alpha fading into genuine transparency. No other visual changes. This asset must be directly compositable on a game's terrain.

rejectedAttempts.reason: Reference-conditioned attempt had painted checkerboard; next attempt had a broad halo. Final regeneration uses no shadow.
rejectedAttempts.initialPrompt: Use case: historical-scene. A transparent-background PNG game sprite of the Chancellor House at Chancellorsville, Virginia, standing in May 1863 before it burned. Use the large principal house in the MIDDLE DISTANCE of the supplied Edwin Forbes May 1 1863 sketch as the architectural reference, not the small foreground log shed. Broad two-and-a-half-story reddish brick tavern/manor with long facade, many white-trimmed sash windows, dark wood shingle side-gabled roof with a few dormers and brick chimney stacks; central and side white porch elements consistent with the reference, taller rear wing. A substantial rural inn, not a grand white-columned plantation fantasy. Change to a bird's-eye three-quarter view looking down 60 degrees, complete roof and front visible. Crisp realistic painterly miniature, muted earth tones, soft light from upper left. One isolated house centered, generous transparent margin, subtle contact shadow. Actual transparent alpha background cutout, no terrain, trees, armies, outbuildings, text or frame. Maintain the main house silhouette from the sketch; uncertain fine details are an illustrative reconstruction.
